bio: Largest city in the City of Latrobe, in the east of the Latrobe Valley in Gippsland, with about 27,000 residents.

bio: Open-air museum of a reconstructed pioneer township on Lloyd Street in Moe, open Wednesday to Sunday.
Former gold-mining town of about 20 residents, with underground mine tours, a goldfields railway and a cemetery.
National park on the Baw Baw Plateau with snowgum forest, granite tors at Mushroom Rocks and snow play in winter.
Alpine resort village at 1450 m in snow gum forest, Melbourne's closest ski resort, with summer walks and biking.
A 25 m waterfall with a viewing platform, reached by a forest walk near Noojee that continues to Amphitheatre Falls.
Cool-temperate rainforest park in South Gippsland with fern-lined creek walks and Corrigan's Suspension Bridge.

bio: Suspension bridge through the rainforest canopy in Tarra-Bulga National Park, with views down into the fern gully.
Corner Inlet town and one of Victoria's earliest ports, settled in 1841, with a maritime museum on Tarraville Road.

bio: Remote East Gippsland park where the Snowy River cuts through Tulloch Ard Gorge, with gorge walks and canoe access.

bio: Plateau park of cool-temperate rainforest, with a rainforest boardwalk, Ocean View Lookout and camping.
Victoria's largest cave system, seen only on guided tours of Royal Cave or Fairy Cave, near Buchan in East Gippsland.
Far-east coastal park near Marlo with wild ocean beaches, Yeerung Gorge rock pools and whale-watching May to October.
Gippsland gorge park with a walk to the Den of Nargun, Billy Goat Bend lookout and Grade III-IV whitewater.
Loop walk in Mitchell River National Park to a waterfall cave said to house the Nargun; please stay out of the cave.

bio: Open-air museum of 1850s Ballarat where you can pan for real gold and take an underground mine tour.
Interpretive centre in Eureka Stockade Memorial Park with an exhibition on the Eureka Rebellion and the Eureka Flag.

bio: Memorial park in Ballarat on the site of the 1854 Eureka Stockade, with interpretive plaques and monuments.

bio: Australia's oldest regional art gallery, founded 1884 and free, currently showing at Backspace Gallery, Mair Street.
gaps: Main building on Lydiard St closed for upgrades; revisit bio when it reopens.

bio: Shallow artificial urban lake beside the suburb of Wendouree, with heritage trams running along its shore.
40-hectare gardens on Lake Wendouree's western shore, a Victorian-style garden flanked by North and South Gardens.
Zoo with over 300 animals, including over 100 free-roaming kangaroos, and hand-feeding of kangaroos and koalas.
Replica medieval castle at Leigh Creek, 8 km east of Ballarat, open to visitors since 1974 with overnight stays.
Volunteer-run museum where heritage trams run around Lake Wendouree and the Botanical Gardens on weekends.
